generator.prompt: Frame-by-frame hand-painted 2D game sprite of Violet, a slender young girl adventurer, side-view profile facing right. She wears a hooded gray robe with a darker waist sash, an ankle-length robe skirt with a slightly darker hem, and goes barefoot with simple ankle wraps. Pale skin, dark hair just visible under the hood, a clearly readable young face in profile with a visible eye, brow, nose and mouth. Realistic child body proportions, about 5.5 head-heights tall, matching the reference turnaround exactly in design, coloring and proportions. Rendered as a single cohesive hand-painted illustration with soft painterly brushwork and visible brush texture, in a muted earthy palette (grays, browns, warm skin tones), NOT a flat vector cutout, in the painted-storybook register of games like Hollow Knight or GRIS. Rising through the air after takeoff, clearly airborne with both feet well off the ground: her legs are beginning to bend and draw up beneath her as she continues to climb, knees lifting, torso now upright with a slight backward lean, head level. Arms are coming down and out from their overhead reach, opening out to the sides, elbows bent. A clear mid-air ascending pose, still rising, between the takeoff extension and the tucked high point of the jump. Full body visible from the top of the hood to the soles of both bare feet, and both hands, entirely inside the canvas with generous empty margin on every side so nothing is cropped. She is airborne and may sit higher or lower in the frame than a grounded pose depending on how high she has risen, but keep her at the exact same body scale (head-to-foot size) as the reference image(s), never bigger or smaller. Fully transparent background with ZERO pixels painted outside her own silhouette: no ground plane, no cast shadow, no vignette, no glow, no halo, no radial light, no gradient, no dark or light background tint of any kind, no border, no text, no watermark, no second copy of the character, no scarf or neck wrap of any kind -- bare gray robe collar at the neck; a separate layer will add the scarf later.
